risks.quote: Overusing AI might potentially weaken critical thinking, reduce research skills and encourage shallow learning as well as shortcuts to the learning process.
Generative AI models are trained on data created by people, therefore may reproduce biases in gender, religion, race, nationality, age, ability, and history.
An AI tool may also provide you with hallucinations of citations, providing a reference to a journal article, law case or other format which doesn’t exist.
Text, media and images generated by AI tools can spread misinformation.
You won’t know what the AI tool has access to or been trained on so you may find the information being provided by the tool is limited or of low quality.
Inputting confidential information into AI tools could breach GDPR and professional society ethics codes.
Generative AI comes with significant environmental costs.

responsibilities.quote: Information provided by AI must be cross-checked against these sources.
Behaving ethically, fairly, honestly, responsibly, and transparently when studying or undertaking and reporting research is essential.
We encourage students are encouraged to use AI tools mindfully due to their environmental impact, in a similar way to the mindful use of paper and printing.
